messages:
alex: Heads-up — we've had 11 ECC/Xid spikes on eu-west1-gpu-03 in the last 6h, and the current autodrain is triggering reimages every 20m.

mari: ugh. that's killing capacity. can we add a debounce? maybe require 3 pulses in 15m before cordon?

jon: +1 to debounce. also we should add a hysteresis window so a node won't reenter rotation for 2h after a drain.

alex: proposal draft:
```
if ecc/xid_pulse_count >= 3 within 900s -> taint node: gpu.health=flaky:NoSchedule
start eviction: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
start slurm: `scontrol update NodeName=<node> State=DRAIN Reason=flaky-gpu`
after cordon, wait 10m for migrations, if pulses continue escalate to owner
recovery: clear taint only after 2h no pulses
rate-limit: max 5 auto-drains per region per hour
```

kai: we should gate on telemetry that the pulses correlate w/ job failures. otherwise we risk false positives for noisy ECC logs.

mari: + add tag for preemptible vs dedicated - preemptible nodes should be evicted earlier, dedicated should have higher threshold.

nodebot: [automation] detected 3 XID spikes on eu-west1-gpu-03 (card 1) at 2264998000,2264998600,2265000500 — recommended auto-cordon

sre-oncall: @alex can we also add a cost check? if region capacity < 5% free, fallback to soft-taint (NoExecute with grace) not immediate drain.

alex: yes. plan: implement pulse-decoder in health-bridge (counter per card), expose `gpu.pulse_count` metric, and a gate service to decide action. I'll prototype rule engine next week.

jon: will help with k8s operator changes (API to taint + annotation with rule-id). also add an audit event so ops can see why node was drained.

mari: ops playbook update pls — steps to manually override and to force bring node back if false-positive.

kai: one more: for SLURM, ensure `scontrol update` is idempotent and that requeue policy respects SLA.

alex: thanks. I'll open a PR with the rule + unit tests. we should run a small canary in us-west2 for 48h before rolling eu-west1.

mari: ack. can we add an observability dashboard: pulses/time, drains/time, reimage_count, capacity_loss?

alex: yep — `grafana/gpu-health-autodrain` obvious panels.

sre-oncall: pinging infra-costs to ensure this doesn't trigger excess fresh GPU provisioning; we want to prefer soft-quarantine over immediate replacement.

jon: ok shipping small canary tomorrow. i'll post results in this thread. :rocket:
